blurb: A held value such as a `Connection[F]` has exactly one owner, and the owner must dispose of it by storing, closing or handing it on. A closure that visits each stored connection (`forEach`, `parTraverse` and their variants) is only lent each one: it may `send`, which leaves the connection owned, but `close` or any transfer would be an owner's act performed on a value the closure does not own. A match guard borrows in the same way, because it runs before its arm is chosen. To close connections, remove them from the store, which closes them, in the owner's code and not in the closure.
example:
conns.forEach((c: Connection[ServerFrame]) => c.close())                          // ✗ `c` is borrowed

conns.forEach((c: Connection[ServerFrame]) => c.send(ServerFrame { text: "closing" }))   // ✓ `send` does not consume
summary: A consuming operation (`close`/`put`/`take`) is called on a *borrowed* held reference — borrows admit only non-consuming operations like `send` (§2.9.3, real-time track slice 2).
